leverage.exposure: None. The balance is positive, there is no leveraged position open, and the recommended action would not open one. The live offer is capped at available cash by design, so even if it wins in full the balance stays positive and no forced sale is triggered before the lock. This matters more than usual right now, because at eleven players there is no body that could be sold to unwind a negative balance without incurring the under-eleven penalty - so leverage is not merely inadvisable this week, it is unavailable. The lock is still most of a week away and no deadline requires a decision in the next couple of hours.

binding_gap: The gap is the compulsory eleventh man. With eleven players and one legal shape, a body who has played no minutes all season is forced into the eleven and contributes nothing. Any twelfth outfielder displaces him, so the entire value of the next purchase is the gap between the newcomer and zero. The forward on the live offer is the largest such gain on the board and also the best points-per-euro on it; the defender held as fallback is the second best. Nothing else listed comes close on either measure.

verdict.headline: No action.
verdict.detail: No action. The Conte raise was executed and his offer is live and still uncontested, resolving early this afternoon UK time. Nothing on the board, in the feed or in the news beats it, and there is no decision to make before it settles. This is a genuinely quiet run and the right response to it is to leave everything alone.

sell.reason: No sale is recommendable this run, and that is a hard constraint rather than a judgement call: at eleven players any sale drops the squad below the legal minimum and incurs the under-eleven penalty, which is larger than every other consideration on this page combined. Two conditional sales are queued behind the live offer. The benched Mainz full-back remains the designated funding sale once the squad is legal at twelve, confirmed again this run as fit but not starting. The Bayern centre-back is now the more interesting case and has been logged as a watch rather than a sale: he is fit and green on every injury list, but a dated matchday sheet leaves him out of the eleven for a second consecutive week, his market value is rising, and selling into strength stays available. He cannot go without a replacement centre-back landing first, because losing him would cost more fielded points than the eleventh man is worth. Re-read Bayern's projected eleven from scratch before the next lock rather than reusing this reading.

buy.reason: The live offer on the Hoffenheim forward stands unchanged and should not be touched. He was re-verified this run on a dated source for the second run running: in the projected eleven in both previews from the club-news feed, no injury, his club's absentee list short and without him, and no flag on the Kickbase record. His listing is still uncontested. A small bonus landed overnight, and raising the bid by it was considered and deliberately declined - the increase is too small to cross any clearing price this league has ever produced, so it would pay a certain cost for a near-zero gain. The Elversberg defender remains the conditional fallback and must not be bid on while the forward's offer is live; he was also re-verified in his club's projected eleven this run. His own match is played before his listing resolves, so unlike the forward his performance is visible before the fallback bid has to land - use it. Everything else on the board fails on points-per-euro, affordability, or both. The newly listed Stuttgart striker is the trap of the week and has been logged as an avoid: a famous name at the largest price on the market, whose average is now a two-match reading rather than a small sample, giving by far the worst cost per fielded point in this ledger, on a falling value, and unaffordable without leverage that could not be unwound before the lock. The cheap end of the board is uniformly bodies with no points record at all, which the ledger has already learned are worth exactly zero fielded points.

standing.name: Maximilian Rohr
standing.why: CONDITIONAL FALLBACK - BID ONLY IF THE CONTE OFFER LOSES. DO NOT BID WHILE THE CONTE OFFER IS LIVE. THE TIMING IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT IS CLEAN: Conte (3204) resolves ~2026-09-05T12:51Z (exs 50780 read at 22:45Z); Rohr resolves ~2026-09-06T00:57Z (exs 94352). That is a TWELVE-HOUR GAP in which the outcome of the Conte bid is known and the cash is either spent or free. So this needs NO leverage, NO sale and NO overlap risk - it is a strictly sequential second attempt at the same money, and it is the answer to the Makengo problem (H5om1wi), where losing the only pre-lock resolver left Georg with cash and nothing to spend it on. THE POINTS CASE: Kickbase listing, prc exactly mv 9.726.134, ofc 0, st 0, stl [], DEF tid 77 = Elversberg (tn first-party). ap 87 off 5039 sec (84 min) in the 3:2 MD1 win over Leverkusen, one yellow, cv 8.900.000 and mv RISING (mvt 1, tfhmvt +74.619). Buying him takes the squad to 12 = 1GK/5DEF/4MID/2ATT, best legal shape 5-3-2, and he enters the eleven: 129 + (Matsima 138, ter Horst 143, Minjae 110, ROHR 87, Widmer 29 = 507) + (Nusa 226, Onyeka 139, Lokonga 44 = 409) + (Gregoritsch 195, Guirassy 180 = 375) = 1420 against 1333 doing nothing = +87. Efficiency 9.726.134 / 87 = 111,8k per point, mid-pack in the squad - better than Minjae 110,2k is not true, but better than Nusa 118,4k, Baumann 133,8k, Guirassy 169,7k and Lokonga 221,2k, and far better than every big-name listing on the board (Koch 184k, Kimmich 198k, Kosugi 351k marginal). FITNESS VERIFIED THIS RUN ON A DATED SOURCE: bundesliga.com voraussichtliche Aufstellungen Spieltag 2, published 04.09.2026, starts him at Gladbach 05.09 13:30Z - "Kristof - Gyamerah, Pinckert, ROHR, Guenther..." - and Elversberg's absentees on that sheet are only Seifert (Syndesmosebandriss) and Zimmerschied (Rueckenprobleme). Absent from ligainsider verletzte-und-gesperrte. WHAT TO BID, AND WHY NOT MERELY mv: per H5om1wi, ofc 0 is a SNAPSHOT AND NOT A FORECAST - Makengo was ofc 1 with Georg alone at 08:45Z and was contested to +60,76% by 16:32Z, eight hours later. Rohr resolves ~26h out, which is more than enough time for a late rival, and a Kickbase listing is HIGHEST-BID-WINS, so raising genuinely buys win probability here (unlike a manager ask). Bid the full cash ceiling 11.343.624 = +16,63% over mv. That is inside the measured contested band and costs at most 1.617.490 over mv if nobody comes - the same insurance trade that B5fsu5e took on Conte, on the same idle cash, for a +87 instead of a +106. ABORT CONDITIONS, ANY ONE OF WHICH KILLS IT: (1) the Conte offer WINS at ~12:51Z - then cash is gone, the squad is 12 with 4-3-3 at 1439, and buying Rohr on top would need ~9,7M of leverage against a realisable unwind of only Amoako 1.569.143 + Widmer 1.852.587 = 3.421.730, leaving an unwindable negative balance that scores ZERO for all of MD3; (2) a source dated 05.09.2026 or later drops him from the Elversberg eleven; (3) his MD2 at Gladbach ends in an injury or a red card - note he kicks off 05.09 13:30Z and the listing resolves ~00:57Z on 06.09, so unlike Conte his match IS visible before the bid must land. Use that: check his MD2 return before bidding.

Replaces closed Bduul6s (price revision only; its points case and fitness case both stand). THE POINTS CASE, UNCHANGED AND RE-VERIFIED: squad is 11 = 1GK/4DEF/4MID/2ATT, only 4-4-2 is legal, so Amoako ap 0 is compulsory in the XI. Conte makes it 12 = 1/4/4/3, legalises 4-3-3, and Amoako drops out: 1333 -> 1439 = +106, the largest single action available. He is also the best efficiency on the board at 9.292.405/106 = 87,7k per point (Rohr 111,8k is the next real candidate). FITNESS RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN on a dated source: Sports Mole preview 04.09.2026 01:36Z starts him in the Hoffenheim XI (Baumann; Coufal, Hajdari, Kabak, Bernardo; Avdullahu, Burger; Wimmer, CONTE, Daghim; Lemperle), TSG absentees only Asllani (knee) and Prass (muscle); Ligainsider verletzte-und-gesperrte lists ZERO Hoffenheim players; Kickbase st 0, stl []. WHY RAISE, AND WHY EXACTLY TO CASH. Georg's +11,92% sits in the bimodal dead space - uncontested listings clear at ~0% (measured 8 for 8), contested ones at +9% to +61%, so it beats only 1 of the 9 measured contested clearings while overpaying 1,1M if nobody comes. At +22,08% it beats 6 of 9. THE DECISIVE ARITHMETIC AGAINST LEVERAGE: the no-points-lost leveraged ceiling (cash + Amoako 1.569.143 = 12.912.767 = +38,97%) beats the SAME 6 of 9, because the next measured clearing above +20,96% is +48,28%. Leverage therefore buys ZERO additional win probability against the measured distribution while opening a negative balance and forcing the Amoako sale that removes the squad's only injury cover. Take the cash ceiling: no sale, balance stays positive, squad ends at 12 with cover. HONEST COST: if the listing stays uncontested he pays 2.051.219 over mv rather than 1.107.595 - an extra 943.624 burned for insurance on the only +106 on the board, against idle cash with no better use before MD3. Even at the full bid he is 107,0k per point, still better than Minjae, Nusa, Baumann, Guirassy and Lokonga.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. There are no manager asks below market value anywhere on the board, so the mechanism the value trade depends on is simply absent - this is a structural absence, not a close call, and no amount of ranking changes it. The feed shows rivals doing it anyway: one manager bought and resold a player inside two minutes for a fraction of a percent, and another did the same and came out behind. That is motion rather than points and is not a model to copy, particularly with the horizon a full week out and the cash already committed to a purchase that is worth real fielded points.

fitness.sweep: Nothing to flag. A full sweep of all eleven squad players plus both buy candidates against a dated matchday sheet, cross-checked against the league-wide injured and suspended table, found no new injury, no suspension, and no dated transfer news for anyone. Three players are out of their club's projected eleven, all by selection rather than fitness, and all three were already known and already recorded. The only in-window dated item on any squad player is an international retirement, which carries no club or fitness implication. The stale traps this ledger has logged were all met and correctly excluded, and the wrong-player trap on the Elversberg midfielder was guarded again and held - he is confirmed in his club's eleven.
